title: Realtime engine
goal: Play, edit, locate and record a session through a real audio device with the realtime data flow of revision 3.1, meeting the M2 exit criteria.
done: Realtime queues, allocation guard, fake and manual devices (#14)
Graph driver: ownership states, duck-and-swap, retirement, watchdog (#16)
Playback engine: play a session document through the graph driver (#24)
Transport orchestration: play, stop, locate with butler handshake and timeout (#26)
Realtime PDC and runtime latency changes (#28)
siann-cli device, play, record and bench commands (#30)

features.title: Playback engine: play a session document through the graph driver
specRefs: Two channels into the audio thread
acceptance: A new module (siann-playback) builds a realtime graph from a session document: per track a streaming player, a track fader and the master bus, plus the entity-to-slot map for the control dispatcher.
FLAC media plays through an in-memory MediaReader until a streaming FLAC reader exists.
Playing a session on the manual device produces output sample-identical to renderOffline for the same document, after the initial fade-in.
A gesture on a track fader moves the sound through the parameter channel, and ending it commits exactly one revision with the final value; reopening the bundle replays it.
No allocations on the audio thread during playback and gestures (allocation guard).

features.title: Structural edits while playing
acceptance: The butler adds and removes disk streams while running; a stream is destroyed only after the graph that used it has been retired and the butler has released it.
Streaming players align to the timeline by position (slot start plus frames consumed versus the block start), so a stream created at publish time plays correctly after a later swap.
Committing a structural edit while playing recompiles and swaps the graph with duck-and-swap; after the swap the output is sample-identical to the offline render of the new document.
Rapid successive edits coalesce: the next compile uses the latest document; no underruns and no audio-thread allocations.

features.title: Transport orchestration: play, stop, locate with butler handshake and timeout
acceptance: locate(target) goes dispatcher -> butler seek -> ready -> paramInbox locate, with a new generation each time; a newer locate cancels an older one.
If the butler is not ready within 1 s the locate proceeds and underruns are counted and reported.
Play from stop is a locate to the current position followed by start.
Tests on the manual and fake devices cover locate during playback, repeated locates, the timeout path and stop/start.

features.title: Meters through meterOutbox
acceptance: Track and master peak and RMS per block go audio -> dispatcher through a latest-value-wins SPSC queue and are readable by a non-realtime consumer with the playhead.
Meter values match values computed offline from the rendered output for a known signal.
A full meter queue drops values and never blocks; no audio-thread allocations.

features.title: Device-side sample-rate conversion
acceptance: When the device cannot run at the session rate, playback goes through output SRC (pull model, FIFO primed to a fixed fill of one graph block) and recording through input SRC.
The SRC library runs allocation-free on the audio thread after setup (allocation guard); r8brain streaming mode, or libsamplerate as the documented fallback.
Sine and impulse tests at 44.1->48 kHz and 48->44.1 kHz meet stated frequency-response, aliasing and alignment limits.
SRC latency is reported to the latency model; the record-offset loopback null test passes through input and output SRC.
The engine exposes a resampling state with device rate, session rate and added latency.

features.title: Realtime PDC and runtime latency changes
acceptance: PDC null tests (direct, send, aux, sidechain) pass when played through the graph driver on the manual device, not only offline.
Changing a node's reported latency during playback recompiles the affected paths; delay lines are rebuilt and the paths ducked and restored; the null tests cancel again after the change.
The offline render and the realtime render of the same graph are identical (parity test).

features.title: siann-cli device, play, record and bench commands
acceptance: siann-cli devices lists output devices (desktop build); play <bundle> [--seconds]; record <bundle> --track <id> [--seconds] commits a take; bench <bundle> --tracks N --buffer F --seconds S reports callbacks, xruns (deadline misses measured against the buffer period) and max callback time as JSON.
Without JUCE the commands report a clear error code instead of failing to build.
A test kills a recording siann-cli process mid-take and verifies the take is listed as pending and recovers on the next open.

exit.text: 32 tracks play for 60 s at 256 samples with zero xruns on the maintainer's machine through the default device (desktop build, siann-cli bench).
exit.how: Run siann-cli bench on a generated 32-track session with the desktop preset; record the JSON in the milestone status.

exit.text: With SRC active (44.1 kHz session on a 48 kHz device), the same bench has zero xruns and the SRC quality and record-offset tests pass.
exit.how: Same bench with a 44.1 kHz session; SRC tests in ctest.

exit.text: Realtime PDC null tests pass, including a latency change during playback.
A fader gesture through the parameter channel commits one revision.
Record 10 minutes and recover after a kill.
exit.how: The long recording test (tagged [long]) and the CLI kill test.

exit.text: Realtime-safety checks are clean: allocation guard on every realtime test, and RealtimeSanitizer where Clang is available.
exit.how: ctest; add a Clang RTSan CI job if the toolchain supports it, otherwise record why not.

killCriterion: Persistent xruns not fixable within the design: stop and hold the Tracktion decision gate with the maintainer.
